'''Erica Gail Klarreich''' is an American [[mathematician]], [[Journalism|journalist]] and [[Popular science|science popularizer]].

==Early life and education==
Klarreich's father was a professor of mathematics, and her mother was a mathematics teacher.<ref>{{cite web |first=Shecky |last=Riemann |url=http://mathtango.blogspot.com.br/2015/04/erica-klarreich-journalistmathematician.html |title=Erica Klarreich... Journalist/Mathematician/Ray Smullyan Fan |date=April 12, 2015 |website=MathTango |type=blog }}</ref>

Klarreich obtained her Ph.D. in mathematics under the guidance of [[Yair Minsky|Yair Nathan Minsky]] at [[Stony Brook University]] in 1997.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=14829|title = Erica Klarreich|author = |date = |publisher = North Dakota State University|accessdate = 4 December 2015|website = The Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref>

==Mathematics==
As a mathematician, Klarreich proved that the boundary of the [[curve complex]] is [[Homeomorphism|homeomorphic]] to the space of ending [[Lamination (topology)|laminations]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Athanase Papadopoulos|title=Handbook of Teichmüller Theory|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sfoDn9rzF4MC&pg=PA339|year=2012|publisher=European Mathematical Society|isbn=978-3-03719-103-3|pages=339}}</ref>

==Popular science writing==
As a popular science writer, Klarreich's work has appeared in publications such as ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', ''[[Scientific American]]'', ''[[New Scientist]]'', and ''[[Quanta Magazine]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.ericaklarreich.com/#about|title = Erica Klarreich|author = |date = |publisher = |accessdate = 4 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.quantamagazine.org/authors/erica-klarreich/|title = Erica Klarreich|author = |date = |publisher = Quanta Magazine|accessdate = 4 December 2015}}</ref> She is one of the winners of the 2021 [[Joint Policy Board for Mathematics]] Communications Award for her popular science writing.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/tools/news?news_id=6418|title=Stats + Stories and Erica Klarreich receive 2021 JPBM Communications Award|publisher=American Mathematical Society|date=October 15, 2020}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
As of 2025, Klarreich lives in [[Berkeley, California]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pressfolios |url=https://ericaklarreich.pressfolios.com/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=ericaklarreich.pressfolios.com}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
===Mathematics===
* "The boundary at infinity of the curve complex and the relative [[Teichmüller space]]"
* "Semiconjugacies between Kleinian group actions on the [[Riemann sphere]]"

* "[http://www.americanscientist.org/libraries/documents/2005711137_306.pdf Foams and honeycombs]", ''[[American Scientist]]'', v. 88, n. 2, pp.&nbsp;152–161, 2000.
* "[http://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v418/n6895/full/418270a.html Quantum cryptography: Can you keep a secret?]", ''Nature'', v. 418, n. 6895, pp.&nbsp;270–272, 2002.
* "[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/num2/2002/4/huygenss-clocks-revisited/1 Huygens's clocks revisited]", ''American Scientist'', v. 90, pp.&nbsp;322–323, 2002.
